# Right ascension and declination

The Orion Nebula is visible to the naked eye as a soft glow in the sword of the hunter. Collimation aligns the primary and secondary mirrors so stars focus to a sharp point. Right ascension is measured in hours along the celestial equator, and declination in degrees north or south of it. Seeing describes air turbulence, while transparency describes haze and humidity.

## Notes

The Orion Nebula is visible to the naked eye as a soft glow in the sword of the hunter. Saturn rings tilt over a fifteen year cycle, so their appearance slowly changes from year to year. Light pollution washes out faint galaxies, so a site with a Bortle class of three or lower is worth the drive. An armillary sphere models the sky with rings for the equator, the ecliptic and the meridian.

A red flashlight keeps night vision intact while reading charts at the eyepiece. The ecliptic is tilted about 23.4 degrees to the celestial equator because of the tilt of the Earth. Light pollution washes out faint galaxies, so a site with a Bortle class of three or lower is worth the drive.
